LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we relate events in a book to our own life experiences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to a text correctly for comprehension
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to a text correctly for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to a text correctly for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to a text correctly for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to a text correctly for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others

What this means
In this part you learn to use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to a text correctly for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to a text correctly for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we relate events in a book to our own life experiences?
2. How can you predict the information in a book even before you read it?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to a text correctly for comprehension.
5. Be able to: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
